title: Prime Arrangements
summary: Calculate the count of permutations for numbers from 1 to n where prime numbers must occupy prime index positions, with the result given modulo 10^9 + 7.
statement: Calculate the count of permutations for numbers from 1 to n where prime numbers must occupy prime index positions, with the result given modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Indices and values are numbered 1 through n.
Prime values must occupy exactly the prime indices.
hints: Count primes from one through n with trial division through each square root.
Prime values can permute among prime positions independently.
Non-prime values likewise permute among the remaining positions.
Multiplying the two factorials counts exactly all valid assignments; apply the modulus.
editorial: Multiplying the two factorials counts exactly all valid assignments; apply the modulus.

tests.explanation: There are three prime and two non-prime slots, giving 3!*2!=12.
The sole non-prime value has one arrangement.
